name: The Geneware Debates: Recorded Sessions, 2194-2197
description: A documentary compilation of the actual recorded public tribunal sessions in which M88's corponation council debated the ethics and legal framework for geneware regulation — three years of hearings distilled into five hours of testimony, argument, and procedural maneuvering. The film requires no narration because the sessions document, in the participants' own words, how geneware ethics were ultimately subordinated to intellectual property law. Considered dry by general audiences but essential by anyone working in bioethics, law, or activism.
cultural_impact: The gap where the excised sessions should be became a known quantity — 'the two missing days' — and their absence is now cited in every serious discussion of geneware consent rights as evidence of institutional bad faith.
story_hooks: Someone has a complete, unedited recording of the excised sessions and is negotiating over what they're worth and to whom.
A participant in the hearings is running for a position within a corponation governance body and their recorded testimony directly contradicts their current public positions.
A researcher cross-referencing the excised footage with the licensed version finds a third version — one that differs from both — suggesting a third party was editing the record simultaneously.
